description: Argues for informative uncertainty in AI answers; distinguishes unchecked facts, probabilistic risk, value disagreements, and ambiguous questions, then proposes evidence receipts.

related_resources.reason: Original TruthfulQA paper; early evidence that imitative model outputs may reproduce common misconceptions.
NIST 2024 treatment of confabulation and information integrity in generative AI.
NIST 2023 criteria for evaluating trustworthiness and risk in context.

historical_claims.anchor: The study was presented at the Association for Computational Linguistics in 2022
The United States National Institute of Standards and Technology addresses related problems in its 2024 generative AI risk profile.

claim_evidence.anchor: NIST uses the term confabulation for generated, confidently presented false content
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: NIST describes confidently presented erroneous material, fabricated reasoning, and citations.

authorship.scope: Original first-person essay narration, illustrative cases, mathematical examples, and non-spoken source companion.

background: No technical background; probability and calibration are explained through the forecast example.
readiness_checks: Distinguish unchecked information, probabilistic risk, normative disagreement, and an ambiguous prompt.
Explain why an unvalidated single-number confidence score does not establish calibrated reliability.
